questions.stem: What are the four main groups of biological molecules?

options.text: Amino acids, fatty acids, sugars, bases

questions.explanation: The four main groups of biological molecules are carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids. These are the large molecules essential for life.

questions.stem: What elements do all organic biological molecules contain?
questions.explanation: All organic biological molecules contain carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen. Proteins and nucleic acids also contain nitrogen, and proteins may contain sulfur.

questions.stem: What type of reaction joins monomers together to form polymers?
questions.explanation: Condensation reactions join monomers together to form polymers by removing a molecule of water. This is the opposite of hydrolysis.

options.text: A large molecule made of repeating units
A small molecule that can join with others to form a polymer

questions.explanation: A monomer is a small, single molecule that can bond with other identical or similar molecules to form a larger polymer through condensation reactions.

questions.stem: What happens during a hydrolysis reaction?

options.text: Monomers join together and water is released
A polymer is broken down into monomers by adding water
Water is removed from the cell

questions.explanation: Hydrolysis is the reverse of condensation. Water is added to break the bonds between monomers, splitting a polymer back into its individual monomer units.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a polymer?
questions.explanation: Starch is a polymer made up of many glucose monomers joined together by condensation reactions. Glucose, amino acids, and fatty acids are all monomers.

questions.stem: Why is carbon able to form the backbone of biological molecules?

options.text: Carbon is the most abundant element on Earth
Carbon can form four covalent bonds, allowing complex chain and ring structures

questions.explanation: Carbon has four electrons in its outer shell, enabling it to form four stable covalent bonds with other atoms. This allows it to form long chains, branched structures, and rings.
